claim: In the Drosophila ovary, two separate niches control germ line stem cell (GSC) self-renewal and differentiation processes.
source: In the Drosophila ovary, two separate niches control germ line stem cell (GSC) self-renewal and differentiation processes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known fact about the Drosophila ovary system.

claim: The cellular redox state regulated by Wnt signaling is critical for the maintenance and function of the differentiation niche to promote GSC progeny differentiation.
source: In this study, we show that the cellular redox state regulated by Wnt signaling is critical for the maintenance and function of the differentiation niche to promote GSC progeny differentiation.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study as stated in the abstract, supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Defective Wnt signaling causes the loss of the differentiation niche and the upregulated BMP signaling in differentiated GSC progeny, thereby disrupting germ cell differentiation.
source: Defective Wnt signaling causes the loss of the differentiation niche and the upregulated BMP signaling in differentiated GSC progeny, thereby disrupting germ cell differentiation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing ISC loss and BMP signaling changes in Wnt signaling-defective conditions.

claim: Wnt signaling controls the expression of multiple glutathione-S-transferase family genes and the cellular redox state.
source: Mechanistically, Wnt signaling controls the expression of multiple glutathione-S-transferase family genes and the cellular redox state.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data showing downregulation of Gst genes in Wnt signaling-defective ISCs and DHE fluorescence measurements.

claim: Wnt2 and Wnt4 function redundantly to maintain active Wnt signaling in the differentiation niche.
source: Finally, Wnt2 and Wnt4 function redundantly to maintain active Wnt signaling in the differentiation niche.
evidence: This is supported by knockdown experiments showing that simultaneous knockdown of both Wnt2 and Wnt4 causes severe defects while single knockdowns do not.

claim: The self-renewal property is controlled in various stem cell systems by interplays between signals from the niche and intrinsic factors.
source: The self-renewal property is controlled in various stem cell systems by interplays between signals from the niche and intrinsic factors (Li and Xie, 2005; Morrison and Spradling, 2008; Losick et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Germ line stem cells (GSCs) in the Drosophila ovary and testis are attractive systems for studying stem cell self-renewal at the molecular and cellular level.
source: Germ line stem cells (GSCs) in the Drosophila ovary and testis are attractive systems for studying stem cell self-renewal at the molecular and cellular level (Fuller and Spradling, 2007; Xie, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: GSC lineage differentiation is controlled extrinsically by a differentiation niche formed by inner germarial sheath cells (ISCs, also known as escort cells).
source: we have recently proposed that GSC lineage differentiation is also controlled extrinsically by a differentiation niche formed by inner germarial sheath cells (ISCs, also known as escort cells).
evidence: This is stated as a recent proposal by the authors, supported by their previous work.

claim: Autocrine Wnt2/4 signaling maintains the differentiation niche by regulating ISC proliferation and survival via redox regulation.
source: In this study, we show that autocrine Wnt2/4 signaling maintains the differentiation niche by regulating ISC proliferation and survival via redox regulation.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by experimental data on ISC proliferation, survival, and redox state.

claim: Two or three GSCs at the tip of the germarium continuously self-renew and generate differentiated GSC daughters, cystoblasts (CBs).
source: In the Drosophila ovary, two or three GSCs at the tip of the germarium, the most anterior region of the Drosophila ovary, continuously self-renew and generate differentiated GSC daughters, cystoblasts (CBs).
evidence: This is a well-established fact about the Drosophila ovary system.

claim: The CBs divide four times synchronously with incomplete cytokinesis to form 2-cell, 4-cell, 8-cell, or 16-cell cysts.
source: The CBs further divide four times synchronously with incomplete cytokinesis to form 2-cell, 4-cell, 8-cell, or 16-cell cysts (de Cuevas et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: GSCs and CBs contain a spherical fusome known as the spectrosome, whereas differentiated germ cell cysts contain a branched fusome.
source: GSCs and their differentiated progeny can be reliably identified by their unique morphology of germ line-specific intracellular organelles known as fusomes: GSCs and CBs contain a spherical fusome known as the spectrosome, whereas differentiated germ cell cysts contain a branched fusome (Lin et al., 1994).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: GSCs can be reliably distinguished from CBs by their direct contact with cap cells.
source: GSCs can be reliably distinguished from CBs by their direct contact with cap cells (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Cap cells function as the self-renewing niche to maintain GSCs by activating BMP signaling and maintaining E-cadherin-mediated cell adhesion.
source: Cap cells function as the self-renewing niche to maintain GSCs by activating BMP signaling and maintaining E-cadherin-mediated cell adhesion (Song et al., 2002; Xie and Spradling, 1998, 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Various classes of intrinsic factors work with BMP signaling and E-cadherin to control GSC self-renewal.
source: In addition, various classes of intrinsic factors work with BMP signaling and E-cadherin to control GSC self-renewal (Xie, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: GSC self-renewal is controlled by coordinated functions of niche-initiated signaling pathways and intrinsic factors.
source: Therefore, GSC self-renewal is controlled by coordinated functions of niche-initiated signaling pathways and intrinsic factors.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the cited literature.

claim: Over 90% of arm and dsh knockdown germaria exhibit the germ cell differentiation defect.
source: Over 90% of arm and dsh knockdown germaria (armKD1 and dshKD1) exhibit the germ cell differentiation defect (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: c587-driven expression of the RNAi lines against different arm or dsh sequences also generates the similar germ cell differentiation defect.
source: Similarly, c587-driven expression of the RNAi lines against different arm or dsh sequences (armKD2 and dshKD2) also generates the similar germ cell differentiation defect (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Wnt ligands bind the receptor complex composed of Frizzled (Fz), Frizzled 2 (Fz2) and Arrow to activate Dsh and stabilize Arm.
source: In Drosophila, Wnt ligands bind the receptor complex composed of Frizzled (Fz), Frizzled 2 (Fz2) and Arrow to activate Dsh and stabilize Arm, which forms a protein complex with a TCF (T Cell Factor)-like Pangolin in the nucleus to activate target gene expression, whereas Axin (Axn) and Shaggy (Sgg) negatively modulate Wnt signaling by promoting Arm degradation (Logan and Nusse, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature describing the canonical Wnt signaling pathway.

claim: Simultaneous knockdown of both fz and fz2 in ISCs recapitulates the germ cell differentiation defect caused by either armKD or dshKD.
source: Simultaneous knockdown down of both fz and fz2 (fzKD+fz2KD) in ISCs recapitulate the germ cell differentiation defect caused by either armKD or dshKD, although either fzKD or fz2KD yields a much weaker germ cell differentiation defect (Figure 1E,F; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E, F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Overexpression of axn and sgg in ISCs leads to the germ cell differentiation defect similar to that caused by armKD and dshKD.
source: Consistently, overexpression of axn and sgg in ISCs also leads to the germ cell differentiation defect similar to that caused by armKD and dshKD (Figure 1E,G,H).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E, G, H.

claim: Wnt signaling is required in ISCs to promote germ cell differentiation.
source: These results indicate that Wnt signaling is required in ISCs to promote germ cell differentiation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing that disrupting Wnt signaling components causes germ cell differentiation defects.

claim: The expression of a constitutively active mutant armS10 (arm*) leads to hyperactive Wnt signaling independently of Wnt ligands.
source: The expression of a constitutively active mutant armS10 (arm*) leads to hyperactive Wnt signaling independently of Wnt ligands (Pai et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: c587-directed arm* expression alone does not cause any obvious GSC maintenance and germ cell differentiation defects, but results in severe egg chamber budding defects likely due to defective follicle cell development.
source: c587-driven arm* expression alone does not cause any obvious GSC maintenance and germ cell differentiation defects, but results in severe egg chamber budding defects likely due to defective follicle cell development (Figure 1I).
evidence: This is supported by experimental observations shown in Figure 1I.

claim: c587-mediated arm* expression can fully rescue the germ cell differentiation defect caused by the two independent dshRNAi knockdowns.
source: Interestingly, c587-mediated arm* expression can fully rescue the germ cell differentiation defect caused by the two independent dshRNAi knockdowns, indicating that Arm functions downstream of Dsh in ISCs to promote germ cell differentiation (Figure 1J–L).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1J-L.

claim: Arm functions downstream of Dsh in ISCs to promote germ cell differentiation.
source: c587-mediated arm* expression can fully rescue the germ cell differentiation defect caused by the two independent dshRNAi knockdowns, indicating that Arm functions downstream of Dsh in ISCs to promote germ cell differentiation (Figure 1J–L).
evidence: This is inferred from the rescue experiment showing that constitutively active Arm can bypass the requirement for Dsh.

claim: Canonical Wnt signaling works in ISCs to promote GSC lineage differentiation.
source: Taken together, our findings demonstrate that canonical Wnt signaling works in ISCs to promote GSC lineage differentiation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing that multiple components of the canonical Wnt pathway are required in ISCs for germ cell differentiation.

claim: The c587-gal4 driver is expressed in somatic precursor cells in the developing female gonad, which give rise to terminal filament, cap cells, adult ISCs, and follicular stem cells.
source: The c587-gal4 driver is known to be expressed in somatic precursor cells in the developing female gonad, which give rise to terminal filament, cap cells, adult ISCs, and follicular stem cells (Zhu and Xie, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: At 25°C, gal80ts is functional to prevent gal4-driven expression of a UAS transgene, but at 29°C, gal80ts is inactivated to allow gal4-driven gene expression.
source: At 25°C, gal80ts is functional to prevent gal4-driven expression of a UAS transgene, but at 29°C, gal80ts is inactivated to allow gal4-driven gene expression (McGuire et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature describing the gal80ts system.

claim: For the c587>>gal80ts control females cultured at 25°C or 29°C as adults for one week, their germaria contain the normal number of CBs.
source: For the c587>>gal80ts control females, which were cultured at 25°C or 29°C as adults for one week, their germaria contain the normal number of CBs (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A, B.

claim: For the c587>>gal80ts UAS-dshRNAi or UAS-armRNAi females cultured at constant 25°C, their germaria contain the normal or close to normal numbers of CBs.
source: Interestingly, for the c587>>gal80ts UAS-dshRNAi or UAS-armRNAi females, which were cultured at constant 25°C, their germaria contain the normal or close to normal numbers of CBs (Figure 2B–F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B-F.

claim: For the c587>>gal80ts UAS-dshRNAi or UAS-armRNAi females shifted from 25°C to 29°C for one week, their germaria contain excess CBs, indicative of the germ cell differentiation defect.
source: In contrast, for the c587>>gal80ts UAS-dshRNAi or UAS-armRNAi females, which were shifted from 25°C to 29°C for one week, their germaria contain excess CBs, indicative of the germ cell differentiation defect (Figure 2B,C′–F′).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B, C'-F'.

claim: Wnt signaling is required in adult ISCs to promote germ cell differentiation.
source: These results demonstrate that Wnt signaling is required in adult ISCs to promote germ cell differentiation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the temperature-shift experiments showing that adult-specific knockdown of Wnt signaling components causes germ cell differentiation defects.

claim: A severe ISC loss causes the germ cell differentiation defect.
source: Our previous studies have shown that a severe ISC loss also causes the similar germ cell differentiation defect (Kirilly et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies by the authors.

claim: PZ1444 expresses nuclear LacZ in ISCs and cap cells, which can be distinguished based on nucleus size and location.
source: PZ1444 expresses nuclear LacZ in ISCs and cap cells, which can be distinguished based on nucleus size and location (Xie and Spradling, 2000).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: In the one-week-old control germaria, PZ1444 labels 30–35 ISCs in addition to cap cells.
source: In the one-week-old control germaria, PZ1444 labels 30–35 ISCs in addition to cap cells (Figure 3A,C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A, C.

claim: In the one-week-old arm and dsh knockdown germaria, only fewer than 5 ISCs remain.
source: In the one-week-old arm and dsh knockdown germaria, only fewer than 5 ISCs remain (Figure 3B–D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B-D.

claim: Overexpression of axn and sgg leads to a severe ISC loss.
source: Consistently, overexpression of axn and sgg also leads to a severe ISC loss (Figure 3E,F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E, F.

claim: Wnt signaling is required to maintain ISCs.
source: These results demonstrate that Wnt signaling is required to maintain ISCs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing that disrupting Wnt signaling causes ISC loss.

claim: arm*-expressing germaria contain significantly more ISCs.
source: Interestingly, arm*-expressing germaria contain significantly more ISCs (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: The one-week-old control germaria contain 32 ISCs, while the one-week-old arm*-expressing germaria carry 130 ISCs.
source: In contrast with the one-week-old control germaria containing 32 ISCs, the one-week-old arm*-expressing germaria carry 130 ISCs (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: c587-mediated axn and sgg knockdown leads to more ISCs.
source: Consistently, c587-mediated axn and sgg knockdown, which increases Wnt-signaling activity (Heslip et al., 1997; Willert et al., 1999), also leads to more ISCs (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and citations to previous literature.

claim: Germ cell differentiation proceeds normally in the germaria carrying extra ISCs.
source: Interestingly, germ cell differentiation proceeds normally in the germaria carrying extra ISCs, suggesting that ISCs provide a permissive environment for germ cell differentiation (Figure 3G; Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental observations shown in Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: ISCs provide a permissive environment for germ cell differentiation.
source: Interestingly, germ cell differentiation proceeds normally in the germaria carrying extra ISCs, suggesting that ISCs provide a permissive environment for germ cell differentiation (Figure 3G; Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that extra ISCs do not disrupt germ cell differentiation.

claim: Defective Wnt signaling significantly decreases ISC proliferation.
source: Based on BrdU-labeling results, defective Wnt signaling significantly decreases ISC proliferation, whereas hyperactive Wnt signaling significantly increases ISC proliferation (Figure 3H–L).
evidence: This is supported by BrdU incorporation data shown in Figure 3H-L.

claim: Hyperactive Wnt signaling significantly increases ISC proliferation.
source: Based on BrdU-labeling results, defective Wnt signaling significantly decreases ISC proliferation, whereas hyperactive Wnt signaling significantly increases ISC proliferation (Figure 3H–L).
evidence: This is supported by BrdU incorporation data shown in Figure 3H-L.

claim: Defective Wnt signaling significantly increases ISC apoptosis.
source: Based on TUNEL-labeling results, defective Wnt signaling significantly increases ISC apoptosis, whereas hyperactive Wnt signaling significantly decreases ISC apoptosis (Figure 3M–Q).
evidence: This is supported by TUNEL labeling data shown in Figure 3M-Q.

claim: Hyperactive Wnt signaling significantly decreases ISC apoptosis.
source: Based on TUNEL-labeling results, defective Wnt signaling significantly increases ISC apoptosis, whereas hyperactive Wnt signaling significantly decreases ISC apoptosis (Figure 3M–Q).
evidence: This is supported by TUNEL labeling data shown in Figure 3M-Q.

claim: Wnt signaling maintains the ISC population by promoting proliferation and increasing survival.
source: These results suggest that Wnt signaling maintains the ISC population by promoting proliferation and increasing survival.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the BrdU and TUNEL labeling experiments.

claim: ISC loss disrupts germ cell differentiation by increasing BMP signaling.
source: Our previous studies have also shown that ISC loss disrupts germ cell differentiation by increasing BMP signaling (Kirilly et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2011; Ma et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies by the authors.

claim: BMP signaling leads to production of phosphorylated Mad (pMad) and activation of Dad-lacZ reporter expression in GSCs.
source: In the Drosophila germarium, BMP signaling leads to production of phosphorylated Mad (pMad) and activation of Dad-lacZ reporter expression in GSCs (Chen and McKearin, 2003; Kai and Spradling, 2003; Casanueva and Ferguson, 2004; Song et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In the control germaria, pMad and Dad-lacZ expression is restricted to GSCs.
source: In the control germaria, pMad and Dad-lacZ expression is restricted to GSCs (Figure 4A,A′,D,D′).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A, A', D, D'.

claim: In the armKD and dshKD germaria, pMad and Dad-lacZ expression is activated in the accumulated CBs locating one to a few cells away from cap cells in addition to GSCs.
source: In the armKD and dshKD germaria, pMad and Dad-lacZ expression is activated in the accumulated CBs locating one to a few cells away from cap cells in addition to GSCs (Figure 4B,B′,C,C′,E,E′,F,F′).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B, B', C, C', E, E', F, F'.

claim: BMP signaling is spread to the differentiation zone in the Wnt signaling-defective germarium.
source: These results indicate that BMP signaling is spread to the differentiation zone in the Wnt signaling-defective germarium.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the pMad and Dad-lacZ expression data.

claim: mRNA levels for the known BMP pathway components, including dpp, gbb, and dally, remain largely unchanged in axn-overexpressing ISCs or dshKD ISCs in comparison with the control.
source: RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) results on the purified ISCs show that mRNA levels for the known BMP pathway components, including dpp, gbb (also encoding a BMP ligand) and dally, remain largely unchanged in axn-overexpressing ISCs or dskKD ISCs in comparison with the control (FKPM = reads per kilobase per million mapped reads).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The heterozygous dpp mutations have partial suppression on the germ cell differentiation defects caused by dshKD.
source: Our CB and GSC quantification results indicate that the heterozygous dpp mutations have partial suppression on the germ cell differentiation defects caused by dshKD, and the suppression is not due to the changes in GSC numbers (50 germaria examined for each genotype).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 4H, H'.

claim: The dpp heterozygous mutation dpphr4 significantly rescues the germ cell differentiation defect caused by dshKD1 and dshKD2.
source: Our results indicate that the dpp heterozygous mutation dpphr4 significantly rescues the germ cell differentiation defect caused by dshKD1 and dshKD2, whereas the dpp heterozygous mutation dpphr56 significantly rescues that caused by dshKD1 but not dshKD2 (Figure 4H).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Wnt signaling in ISCs regulates germ cell differentiation partly by preventing BMP signaling in the differentiation niche.
source: These results suggest that Wnt signaling in ISCs regulates germ cell differentiation partly by preventing BMP signaling in the differentiation niche.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the genetic interaction experiments with dpp mutations.

claim: Long ISC cellular processes are required to promote germ cell differentiation.
source: Long ISC cellular processes are also required to promote germ cell differentiation (Kirilly et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: In the control germaria, ISC cellular processes wrap up differentiated germ cells.
source: In the control germaria, ISC cellular processes wrap up differentiated germ cells (Figure 4I,I′).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4I, I'.

claim: Cellular processes in the remaining ISCs of the armKD and dshKD germaria fail to extend into the accumulated CBs.
source: In contrast, cellular processes in the remaining ISCs of the armKD and dshKD germaria fail to extend into the accumulated CBs (Figure 4J–K′).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4J-K'.

claim: Wnt signaling is required to maintain ISC cellular processes.
source: These results indicate that Wnt signaling is required to maintain ISC cellular processes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that Wnt signaling-defective ISCs lack long cellular processes.

claim: A recent study proposes that Wnt signaling upregulates piwi expression in ISCs, thereby promoting germ cell differentiation.
source: A recent study proposes that Wnt signaling upregulates piwi expression in ISCs, thereby promoting germ cell differentiation (Hamada-Kawaguchi et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Piwi protein shows comparable expression levels among the examined control ISCs, armKD1 ISCs, armKD2 ISCs, and dshKD2 ISCs.
source: Piwi protein shows comparable expression levels among the examined 203 control ISCs, 48 armKD1 ISCs, 58 armKD2 ISCs, and 46 dshKD2 ISCs (Figure 5A–D).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 5A-D.

claim: Piwi protein levels are significantly elevated in the dshKD1 ISCs in comparison with the control ISCs.
source: Surprisingly, Piwi protein levels are significantly elevated in the dshKD1 ISCs (93 examined) in comparison with the control ISCs (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The piwi mRNA levels are slightly upregulated in the axnOE ISCs and are significantly upregulated in the dshKD ISCs in comparison to the control ISCs.
source: The RNA-seq results show that the piwi mRNA levels are slightly upregulated in the axnOE ISCs and are significantly upregulated in the dshKD ISCs in comparison to the control ISCs (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Wnt signaling promotes germ cell differentiation unlikely by maintaining Piwi expression in ISCs.
source: Therefore, our results indicate that Wnt signaling promotes germ cell differentiation unlikely by maintaining Piwi expression in ISCs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Piwi protein and mRNA expression data showing no downregulation in Wnt signaling-defective ISCs.

claim: Wnt signaling possibly works with Piwi in an unknown means to promote germ cell differentiation.
source: However, Wnt signaling possibly works with Piwi in an unknown means to promote germ cell differentiation because the loss of their functions in ISCs leads to similar germ cell differentiation defects (Jin et al., 2013; Hamada-Kawaguchi et al., 2014; Ma et al., 2014).
evidence: This is speculated based on the similar phenotypes caused by loss of Wnt signaling and Piwi, supported by citations.

claim: Four Gst genes, GstD2, GstD4, GstD10, and GstE3, decrease their mRNA expression levels significantly in both dshKD- and axn-overexpressing ISCs in comparison with the control.
source: Our RNA-seq results also show that four Gst genes, GstD2, GstD4, GstD10, and GstE3, decrease their mRNA expression levels significantly in both dshKD- and axn-overexpressing ISCs in comparison with the control (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: GST proteins comprise a family of eukaryotic metabolic enzymes for eliminating hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) and catalyzing the conjugation of the reduced form of glutathione (GSH) to oxidized substrates for the purpose of detoxification.
source: GST proteins comprise a family of eukaryotic metabolic enzymes for eliminating hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) and catalyzing the conjugation of the reduced form of glutathione (GSH) to oxidized substrates for the purpose of detoxification.
evidence: This is established knowledge about GST protein function.

claim: Downregulated expression of the Gst genes in the Wnt signaling-defective ISCs might cause the increase in cellular reactive oxygen species (ROS).
source: Thus, downregulated expression of the Gst genes in the Wnt signaling-defective ISCs might cause the increase in cellular reactive oxygen species (ROS), which can be detected by dihydroethidium (DHE) fluorescence.
evidence: This is inferred from the known function of GST proteins and the observed downregulation of Gst genes.

claim: In the anterior half of control germaria, ISCs and underneath differentiating germ cells show low DHE fluorescence, indicating that these cells have low cellular ROS levels.
source: In the anterior half of control germaria, ISCs and underneath differentiating germ cells show low DHE fluorescence, indicating that these cells have low cellular ROS levels, including ISCs (Figure 6B; Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B′).
evidence: This is supported by DHE fluorescence data shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, B'.

claim: dshKD and armKD ISCs elevate DHE fluorescence, and germ cells underneath also increase DHE fluorescence.
source: In contrast, dshKD and armKD ISCs elevate DHE fluorescence, and germ cells underneath also increase DHE fluorescence, further supporting the idea that defective Wnt signaling results in the increased cellular ROS in ISCs and their interacting germ cells (Figure 6B′; Figure 6—figure supplement 1C–G).
evidence: This is supported by DHE fluorescence data shown in Figure 6B' and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C-G.

claim: Defective Wnt signaling results in the increased cellular ROS in ISCs and their interacting germ cells.
source: In contrast, dshKD and armKD ISCs elevate DHE fluorescence, and germ cells underneath also increase DHE fluorescence, further supporting the idea that defective Wnt signaling results in the increased cellular ROS in ISCs and their interacting germ cells (Figure 6B′; Figure 6—figure supplement 1C–G).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the DHE fluorescence data.

claim: GST2 is a distinct GST family member from the GST-D family members and has similar function in regulating the cellular redox state.
source: As a distinct GST family member from the GST-D family members, GST2 has similar function in regulating the cellular redox state (Singh et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: GST2 overexpression in the dshKD ISCs can restore low DHE fluorescence in the anterior half of the germaria.
source: Consistently, GST2 overexpression in the dshKD ISCs can also restore low DHE fluorescence in the anterior half of the germaria, suggesting that Wnt signaling controls the cellular redox state in ISCs, GSCs, and early GSC progeny by regulating Gst gene expression (Figure 6B″; Figure 6—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is supported by DHE fluorescence data shown in Figure 6B'' and Figure 6—figure supplement 1H.

claim: Wnt signaling controls the cellular redox state in ISCs, GSCs, and early GSC progeny by regulating Gst gene expression.
source: Consistently, GST2 overexpression in the dshKD ISCs can also restore low DHE fluorescence in the anterior half of the germaria, suggesting that Wnt signaling controls the cellular redox state in ISCs, GSCs, and early GSC progeny by regulating Gst gene expression (Figure 6B″; Figure 6—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is inferred from the rescue of ROS levels by GST2 overexpression.

claim: Catalase (CAT) can help eliminate cellular H2O2 by converting it to free oxygen and water.
source: Catalase (CAT) can also help eliminate cellular H2O2 by converting it to free oxygen and water.
evidence: This is established knowledge about catalase function.

claim: CAT overexpression in the dshKD ISCs restores low cellular ROS in the anterior half of the germaria.
source: As expected, CAT overexpression in the dshKD ISCs also restores low cellular ROS in the anterior half of the germaria (Figure 6B′″; Figure 6—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: This is supported by DHE fluorescence data shown in Figure 6B''' and Figure 6—figure supplement 1I.

claim: Wnt signaling regulates the cellular redox state in ISCs by controlling Gst gene expression.
source: These results suggest that Wnt signaling regulates the cellular redox state in ISCs by controlling Gst gene expression.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the rescue experiments with GST2 and CAT overexpression.

claim: GST2, CAT, and SOD1 overexpression in the dshKD ISCs drastically and significantly reduces CB numbers in the germaria.
source: GST2, CAT, and SOD1 overexpression in the dshKD ISCs drastically and significantly reduces CB numbers in the germaria, but does not change GSC numbers significantly, indicating that increased cellular ROS levels in dshKD ISCs are largely responsible for the germ cell differentiation defect (Figure 6C–F; Figure 6—figure supplement 2D–G).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 6C-F and Figure 6—figure supplement 2D-G.

claim: Increased cellular ROS levels in dshKD ISCs are largely responsible for the germ cell differentiation defect.
source: GST2, CAT, and SOD1 overexpression in the dshKD ISCs drastically and significantly reduces CB numbers in the germaria, but does not change GSC numbers significantly, indicating that increased cellular ROS levels in dshKD ISCs are largely responsible for the germ cell differentiation defect (Figure 6C–F; Figure 6—figure supplement 2D–G).
evidence: This is inferred from the rescue of the differentiation defect by ROS-reducing enzymes.

claim: GST2, CAT, and SOD1 overexpression in the dshKD ISCs significantly and drastically rescue the ISC number, but not to the wild-type ISC number.
source: Similarly, GST2, CAT, and SOD1 overexpression in the dshKD ISCs significantly and drastically rescue the ISC number, but not to the wild-type ISC number, indicating that increased ROS is at least partly responsible for the loss of dshKD ISCs (Figure 6G–J; Figure 6—figure supplement 2H–M).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 6G-J and Figure 6—figure supplement 2H-M.

claim: Increased ROS is at least partly responsible for the loss of dshKD ISCs.
source: Similarly, GST2, CAT, and SOD1 overexpression in the dshKD ISCs significantly and drastically rescue the ISC number, but not to the wild-type ISC number, indicating that increased ROS is at least partly responsible for the loss of dshKD ISCs (Figure 6G–J; Figure 6—figure supplement 2H–M).
evidence: This is inferred from the partial rescue of ISC numbers by ROS-reducing enzymes.

claim: Wnt signaling in ISCs maintains the reduced redox state, which is partly responsible for ISC maintenance and germ cell differentiation.
source: Taken together, these results demonstrate that Wnt signaling in ISCs maintains the reduced redox state, which is partly responsible for ISC maintenance and germ cell differentiation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the rescue experiments showing that reducing ROS can rescue both ISC loss and germ cell differentiation defects.

claim: GstD2 is the most abundantly expressed Gst gene in ISCs.
source: Our RNA-seq results indicate that GstD2 is the most abundantly expressed Gst genes in ISCs.
evidence: This is based on RNA-seq data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: GstD2 is the most severely downregulated Gst gene in the Wnt signaling-defective ISCs.
source: In addition, it is also the most severely downregulated Gst gene in the Wnt signaling-defective ISCs, which prompted us to further investigate its function in promoting germ cell differentiation (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is based on RNA-seq data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: GstD2KD1 efficiently knocks down GstD2 mRNA but GstD2KD2 does not based on quantitative RT-PCR results on the purified ISCs.
source: We generated two independent RNAi lines against GstD2, among which Line 1 (GstD2KD1) efficiently knocks down GstD2 mRNA but Line 2 (GstD2KD2) does not based on quantitative RT-PCR results on the purified ISCs (Figure 6K).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative RT-PCR data shown in Figure 6K.

claim: The GstD2KD1 germaria contain two CBs on average, which are significantly more than the control.
source: In contrast with the control germaria containing one CB on average, the GstD2KD1 germaria contain two CBs, which are significantly more than the control (Figure 6L,O).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 6L, O.

claim: c587-mediated expression of Gst2 and Cat can rescue the moderate germ cell differentiation defect caused by GstD2KD1.
source: Interestingly, c587-mediated expression of Gst2 and Cat can also rescue the moderate germ cell differentiation defect caused by GstD2KD1, indicating that the differentiation defect is caused by GstD2 knockdown in ISCs (Figure 6O).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 6O.

claim: Gst genes are required in ISCs to promote germ cell differentiation.
source: Considering the fact that additional three Gst genes are downregulated in the Wnt signaling-defective ISCs, these results indicate that Gst genes are required in ISCs to promote germ cell differentiation.
evidence: This is inferred from the GstD2 knockdown phenotype and the fact that multiple Gst genes are downregulated in Wnt signaling-defective ISCs.

claim: Both Cat and Gst genes work together to remove cellular hydrogen peroxide (H2O2).
source: Both Cat and Gst genes work together to remove cellular hydrogen peroxide (H2O2).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the function of Cat and Gst genes.

claim: The c587-mediated Cat knockdown (CatKD) germaria behave like the control germaria, containing one CB on average.
source: The c587-mediated Cat knockdown (CatKD) germaria behave like the control germaria, containing one CB on average (Figure 6M,O).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 6M, O.

claim: c587-mediated CatKD significantly enhances the germ cell differentiation defect caused by GstD2KD1.
source: Interestingly, c587-mediated CatKD significantly enhances the germ cell differentiation defect caused by GstD2KD1, and consequently the double knockdown germaria accumulate significantly more CBs than the single knockdown germaria (Figure 6N,O).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 6N, O.

claim: The CatKD germaria carry a normal number of ISCs.
source: In addition, the CatKD germaria carry a normal number of ISCs, whereas the GstD2KD germaria carry slightly fewer ISCs (Figure 6P,Q,S).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 6P, Q, S.

claim: The GstD2KD germaria carry slightly fewer ISCs.
source: In addition, the CatKD germaria carry a normal number of ISCs, whereas the GstD2KD germaria carry slightly fewer ISCs (Figure 6P,Q,S).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 6P, Q, S.

claim: The GstD2KD1 CatKD germaria carry significantly fewer ISCs than the GstD1KD1 or CatKD germaria.
source: Consistently, the GstD2KD1 CatKD germaria carry significantly fewer ISCs than the GstD1KD1 or CatKD germaria (Figure 6R,S).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 6R, S.

claim: Cat and Gst genes work together in ISCs to maintain ISCs and promote germ cell differentiation.
source: These results indicate that Cat and Gst genes work together in ISCs to maintain ISCs and promote germ cell differentiation, and further suggest that redox control is important for ISC maintenance.
evidence: This is inferred from the genetic interaction between Cat and GstD2 knockdowns.

claim: Redox control is important for ISC maintenance.
source: These results indicate that Cat and Gst genes work together in ISCs to maintain ISCs and promote germ cell differentiation, and further suggest that redox control is important for ISC maintenance.
evidence: This is inferred from the ISC loss phenotype in GstD2KD1 CatKD germaria.

claim: Four Wnt-like genes are expressed in the purified ISCs, but wingless shows little expression.
source: Our RNA-seq results indicate that four Wnt-like genes are expressed in the purified ISCs, but wingless shows little expression (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Wnt2 and Wnt4 are expressed at high levels in ISCs, whereas Wnt5 and Wnt6 are present in much lower levels.
source: Wnt2 and Wnt4 are expressed at high levels, whereas Wnt5 and Wnt6 are present in much lower levels (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: wnt4 mRNAs are restricted to ISCs, whereas wnt2 mRNAs are also present in ISCs.
source: A recent study has shown that wnt4 mRNAs are indeed restricted to ISCs, whereas wnt2 mRNAs are also present in ISCs (Luo et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a recent study.

claim: Knocking down Wnt2 or Wnt4 alone in ISCs by two or three independent RNAi lines results in no or slight germ cell differentiation defect based on CB numbers.
source: Knocking down Wnt2 or Wnt4 alone in ISCs by two or three independent RNAi lines results in no or slight germ cell differentiation defect based on CB numbers (Figure 7B–D).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 7B-D.

claim: Simultaneous knockdown of Wnt2 and Wnt4 via different combinations of RNAi lines leads to a severe germ cell differentiation defect, which is similar to that caused by dshKD or armKD.
source: Consistent with the idea that Wnt2 and Wnt4 function redundantly in ISCs, simultaneous knockdown of Wnt2 and Wnt4 via different combinations of RNAi lines leads to a severe germ cell differentiation defect, which is similar to that caused by dshKD or armKD (Figure 7D–H).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 7D-H.

claim: Wnt2 and Wnt4 in ISCs serve as redundant autocrine signals for promoting germ cell differentiation.
source: These results demonstrate that Wnt2 and Wnt4 in ISCs serve as redundant autocrine signals for promoting germ cell differentiation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the double knockdown experiments showing severe defects only when both Wnt2 and Wnt4 are knocked down.

claim: Autocrine Wnt2 and Wnt4 signals control ISC maintenance and promote germ cell differentiation at least in part by maintaining the reduced redox state and preventing BMP signaling.
source: A schematic diagram showing that autocrine Wnt2 and Wnt4 signals control ISC maintenance and promote germ cell differentiation at least in part by maintaining the reduced redox state and preventing BMP signaling.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings shown in Figure 7I.

claim: Wnt signaling is required in ISCs for their maintenance by promoting cell proliferation and survival.
source: First, Wnt signaling is required in ISCs for their maintenance by promoting cell proliferation and survival.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the BrdU and TUNEL experiments.

claim: Defective Wnt signaling causes a severe ISC loss, thereby preventing germ cell differentiation.
source: Defective Wnt signaling causes a severe ISC loss, thereby preventing germ cell differentiation.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the ISC quantification experiments.

claim: Wnt signaling is required to maintain the reduced redox state by sustaining the expression of Gst genes.
source: Second, Wnt signaling is required to maintain the reduced redox state by sustaining the expression of Gst genes.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the RNA-seq and DHE fluorescence experiments.

claim: This study has revealed a novel connection between Wnt signaling and redox control.
source: This represents a novel connection between Wnt signaling and redox control.
evidence: This is stated as a novel finding of the study.

claim: The reduced redox state is critical for ISC survival and thus for promoting germ cell differentiation.
source: In addition, this study has also revealed that the reduced redox state is critical for ISC survival and thus for promoting germ cell differentiation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the rescue experiments with ROS-reducing enzymes.

claim: Wnt signaling in ECs promotes GSC progeny differentiation partly by repressing BMP signaling in differentiated GSC progeny.
source: Third, Wnt signaling in ECs promotes GSC progeny differentiation partly by repressing BMP signaling in differentiated GSC progeny.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the pMad and Dad-lacZ expression experiments and genetic interaction with dpp mutations.

claim: Wnt signaling has been shown to control stem cell self-renewal directly.
source: Wnt signaling has been shown to control stem cell self-renewal directly (Holland et al., 2013), whereas ROS has shown to prime hematopoietic progenitor differentiation in Drosophila (Owusu-Ansah and Banerjee, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: ROS has been shown to prime hematopoietic progenitor differentiation in Drosophila.
source: Wnt signaling has been shown to control stem cell self-renewal directly (Holland et al., 2013), whereas ROS has shown to prime hematopoietic progenitor differentiation in Drosophila (Owusu-Ansah and Banerjee, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: This study has demonstrated the importance of Wnt signaling in maintaining the GSC differentiation niche by reducing ROS and thus promoting GSC lineage differentiation.
source: This study has demonstrated the importance of Wnt signaling in maintaining the GSC differentiation niche by reducing ROS and thus promoting GSC lineage differentiation.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings of the study.

claim: This study has identified critical signals for maintaining the GSC differentiation niche and has revealed a novel function of Wnt signaling in the regulation of cellular redox.
source: Therefore, this study not only has identified critical signals for maintaining the GSC differentiation niche but also has revealed a novel function of Wnt signaling in the regulation of cellular redox.
evidence: This is a summary of the main contributions of the study.

claim: Autocrine Wnt signaling controls ISC maintenance, thereby promoting germ cell differentiation.
source: This study has demonstrated that autocrine Wnt signaling controls ISC maintenance, thereby promoting germ cell differentiation.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings of the study.

claim: Canonical Wnt signaling is required in ISCs to promote germ cell differentiation.
source: First, canonical Wnt signaling is required in ISCs to promote germ cell differentiation.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the knockdown and overexpression experiments of Wnt pathway components.

claim: c587-mediated knockdown of Wnt signal transducers Fz/fz2, dsh, and arm as well as c587-directed overexpression of Wnt signaling inhibitors sgg and axn leads to similar germ cell differentiation defects.
source: c587-mediated knockdown of Wnt signal transducers Fz/fz2, dsh, and arm as well as c587-directed overexpression of Wnt signaling inhibitors sgg and axn leads to similar germ cell differentiation defects.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the knockdown and overexpression experiments.

claim: c587-directed overexpression of a constitutively active form of arm* can fully rescue the germ cell differentiation defect caused by dsh knockdown.
source: Moreover, c587-directed overexpression of a constitutively active form of arm* can fully rescue the germ cell differentiation defect caused by dsh knockdown.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the rescue experiments.

claim: Wnt signaling maintains ISCs by promoting proliferation and survival.
source: Second, Wnt signaling maintains ISCs by promoting proliferation and survival.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the BrdU and TUNEL experiments.

claim: c587-mediated knockdown of dsh and arm leads to a severe ISC loss.
source: c587-mediated knockdown of dsh and arm leads to a severe ISC loss, whereas c587-mediated knockdown of sgg and axn or c587-directed arm* overexpression expands the ISC population.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the ISC quantification experiments.

claim: c587-mediated knockdown of sgg and axn or c587-directed arm* overexpression expands the ISC population.
source: c587-mediated knockdown of dsh and arm leads to a severe ISC loss, whereas c587-mediated knockdown of sgg and axn or c587-directed arm* overexpression expands the ISC population.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the ISC quantification experiments.

claim: Hyperactive Wnt signaling increases ISC proliferation and decreases apoptosis, whereas Wnt signaling downregulation increases ISC apoptosis and decreases proliferation.
source: In addition, hyperactive Wnt signaling increases ISC proliferation and decreases apoptosis, whereas Wnt signaling downregulation increases ISC apoptosis and decreases proliferation.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the BrdU and TUNEL experiments.

claim: Canonical Wnt signaling maintains the differentiation niche by promoting ISC proliferation and survival.
source: Thus, canonical Wnt signaling maintains the differentiation niche by promoting ISC proliferation and survival.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ISC proliferation and survival experiments.

claim: ISC-expressing Wnt2 and Wnt4 function redundantly in the differentiation niche to promote germ cell differentiation.
source: Third, ISC-expressing Wnt2 and Wnt4 function redundantly in the differentiation niche to promote germ cell differentiation.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the Wnt2 and Wnt4 knockdown experiments.

claim: wnt2 and wnt4 mRNAs are present in the purified ISCs at high levels, while other wnt genes are expressed at much lower levels.
source: Our RNA-seq results show that wnt2 and wnt4 mRNAs are present in the purified ISCs at high levels, while other wnt genes are expressed at much lower levels.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data.

claim: c587-mediated wnt2 and wnt4 double knockdown results in more severe germ cell differentiation defects than wnt2 or wnt4 single knockdown.
source: c587-mediated wnt2 and wnt4 double knockdown results in more severe germ cell differentiation defects than wnt2 or wnt4 single knockdown.
evidence: This is supported by quantification data from the knockdown experiments.

claim: Piwi is required in the differentiation niche for promoting germ cell differentiation partly by repressing dpp expression.
source: Piwi has recently been shown to be required in the differentiation niche for promoting germ cell differentiation partly by repressing dpp expression (Jin et al., 2013; Ma et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: A recent study proposes that Wnt signaling controls germ cell differentiation by regulating piwi expression.
source: Although a recent study proposes that Wnt signaling controls germ cell differentiation by regulating piwi expression (Hamada-Kawaguchi et al., 2014), this study shows that Piwi protein and mRNAs are not downregulated in Wnt signaling-defective ISCs, suggesting that Wnt signaling does not sustain piwi expression in the differentiation niche to promote GSC progeny differentiation.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Piwi protein and mRNAs are not downregulated in Wnt signaling-defective ISCs.
source: Although a recent study proposes that Wnt signaling controls germ cell differentiation by regulating piwi expression (Hamada-Kawaguchi et al., 2014), this study shows that Piwi protein and mRNAs are not downregulated in Wnt signaling-defective ISCs, suggesting that Wnt signaling does not sustain piwi expression in the differentiation niche to promote GSC progeny differentiation.
evidence: This is supported by Piwi protein quantification and RNA-seq data.

claim: Wnt signaling does not sustain piwi expression in the differentiation niche to promote GSC progeny differentiation.
source: Although a recent study proposes that Wnt signaling controls germ cell differentiation by regulating piwi expression (Hamada-Kawaguchi et al., 2014), this study shows that Piwi protein and mRNAs are not downregulated in Wnt signaling-defective ISCs, suggesting that Wnt signaling does not sustain piwi expression in the differentiation niche to promote GSC progeny differentiation.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Piwi levels are not decreased in Wnt signaling-defective ISCs.

claim: GstD2, GstD4, GstD10, and GstE3 mRNA expression levels are significantly downregulated in the purified Wnt signaling-defective ISCs in comparison with the control ISCs.
source: First, our RNA-seq results show that GstD2, GstD4, GstD10, and GstE3 mRNA expression levels are significantly downregulated in the purified Wnt signaling-defective ISCs in comparison with the control ISCs.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data.

claim: Defective Wnt signaling in ISCs elevates ROS levels in themselves and underneath germ cells.
source: Second, defective Wnt signaling in ISCs elevates ROS levels in themselves and underneath germ cells, indicating that Wnt signaling is required in the differentiation niche to maintain low ROS levels.
evidence: This is supported by DHE fluorescence data.

claim: Wnt signaling is required in the differentiation niche to maintain low ROS levels.
source: Second, defective Wnt signaling in ISCs elevates ROS levels in themselves and underneath germ cells, indicating that Wnt signaling is required in the differentiation niche to maintain low ROS levels.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that defective Wnt signaling increases ROS levels.

claim: c587-directed GST2, SOD1, and CAT overexpression can dramatically suppress the ROS elevation, the germ cell differentiation retardation, and the ISC loss caused by defective Wnt signaling.
source: Third, c587-directed GST2, SOD1, and CAT overexpression can dramatically suppress the ROS elevation, the germ cell differentiation retardation, and the ISC loss caused by defective Wnt signaling, indicating that ROS elevation is responsible for the germ cell differentiation defect and the ISC loss.
evidence: This is supported by rescue experiment data.

claim: ROS elevation is responsible for the germ cell differentiation defect and the ISC loss.
source: Third, c587-directed GST2, SOD1, and CAT overexpression can dramatically suppress the ROS elevation, the germ cell differentiation retardation, and the ISC loss caused by defective Wnt signaling, indicating that ROS elevation is responsible for the germ cell differentiation defect and the ISC loss.
evidence: This is inferred from the rescue of phenotypes by ROS-reducing enzymes.

claim: c587-mediated knockdown of GstD2 and Cat results in the ISC loss and the germ cell differentiation defect.
source: Finally, c587-mediated knockdown of GstD2 and Cat results in the ISC loss and the germ cell differentiation defect, indicating that ROS elevation in ISCs is sufficient to cause ISC loss and retard germ cell differentiation.
evidence: This is supported by knockdown experiment data.

claim: ROS elevation in ISCs is sufficient to cause ISC loss and retard germ cell differentiation.
source: Finally, c587-mediated knockdown of GstD2 and Cat results in the ISC loss and the germ cell differentiation defect, indicating that ROS elevation in ISCs is sufficient to cause ISC loss and retard germ cell differentiation.
evidence: This is inferred from the phenotypes caused by GstD2 and Cat knockdown.

claim: This study has, for the first time, demonstrated that autocrine Wnt signaling controls cellular redox state in the differentiation niche and thus promotes germ cell differentiation.
source: This study has, for the first time, demonstrated that autocrine Wnt signaling controls cellular redox state in the differentiation niche and thus promotes germ cell differentiation.
evidence: This is stated as a novel finding of the study.

claim: Various studies have revealed a number of important signaling pathways and factors in ISCs to promote germ cell differentiation by maintaining ISC cellular process-mediated germ cell–soma interaction and preventing BMP signaling.
source: So far, various studies have revealed a number of important signaling pathways and factors in ISCs to promote germ cell differentiation by maintaining ISC cellular process-mediated germ cell–soma interaction and preventing BMP signaling (Xie, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a review article.

claim: Wnt signaling is required for preventing BMP signaling in differentiated germ cells and for maintaining long ISC cellular processes.
source: This study shows that Wnt signaling is required for preventing BMP signaling in differentiated germ cells and for maintaining long ISC cellular processes.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the pMad/Dad-lacZ expression and ISC cellular process experiments.

claim: Rho, Eggless, Woc, Lsd1, Piwi, EGFR signaling, and ecdysone signaling have been shown to be required in ISCs to maintain long ISC cellular processes encasing germ cells.
source: Rho, Eggless, Woc, Lsd1, Piwi, EGFR signaling, and ecdysone signaling have been shown to be required in ISCs to maintain long ISC cellular processes encasing germ cells (Schultz et al., 2002; Kirilly et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2011; Eliazer et al., 2014; Ma et al., 2014; Maimon et al., 2014; Konig and Shcherbata, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Properly differentiated germ cells are required to maintain long ISC cellular processes.
source: Since properly differentiated germ cells are also required to maintain long ISC cellular processes (Kirilly et al., 2011), it is difficult to distinguish the cause and effect of the germ cell differentiation defect and the ISC cellular process loss.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Three known strategies operate in the differentiation niche to prevent BMP signaling, thereby producing a permissive environment for germ cell differentiation.
source: In contrast, three known strategies operate in the differentiation niche to prevent BMP signaling, thereby producing a permissive environment for germ cell differentiation.
evidence: This is a summary of previous findings from the literature.

claim: Lsd1, Rho, and Piwi are required in ISCs to repress dpp mRNA expression, thereby directly preventing BMP signaling in the differentiation niche.
source: First, Lsd1, Rho, and Piwi are required in ISCs to repress dpp mRNA expression, thereby directly preventing BMP signaling in the differentiation niche (Eliazer et al., 2011; Kirilly et al., 2011; Jin et al., 2013; Ma et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: dpp encodes a BMP ligand, which activates BMP signaling important for GSC self-renewal.
source: dpp encodes a BMP ligand, which activates BMP signaling important for GSC self-renewal (Xie and Spradling, 1998).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Rho, Eggless, and EGFR signaling function in ISCs to repress the expression of dally, preventing BMP diffusion from the self-renewal niche to the differentiation niche.
source: Second, Rho, Eggless, and EGFR signaling function in ISCs to repress the expression of dally, preventing BMP diffusion from the self-renewal niche to the differentiation niche (Liu et al., 2010; Kirilly et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Dally is a proteoglycan protein facilitating BMP differentiation and signaling, and is expressed in cap cells to restrict BMP signaling to GSCs.
source: Dally, which is a proteoglycan protein facilitating BMP differentiation and signaling, is expressed in cap cells, the GSC self-renewal niche, to restrict BMP signaling to GSCs (Akiyama et al., 2008; Guo and Wang, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: A recent study has proposed that cap cell-initiated Wnt signaling maintains the expression of tkv encoding a type I BMP receptor in ISCs, thereby preventing BMP signaling in differentiated germ cells.
source: Third, a recent study has proposed that cap cell-initiated Wnt signaling maintains the expression of tkv encoding a type I BMP receptor in ISCs, thereby preventing BMP signaling in differentiated germ cells (Luo et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a recent study.

claim: The findings from this study have supported the idea that autocrine Wnt signaling in ISCs promotes GSC progeny differentiation partly by repressing BMP signaling.
source: Our findings from this study have also supported the idea that autocrine Wnt signaling in ISCs promotes GSC progeny differentiation partly by repressing BMP signaling.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the BMP signaling experiments.

claim: The findings have argued that inactivating Wnt signaling does not regulate the mRNA expression levels of tkv and other BMP pathway components in ISCs.
source: However, our findings have also argued that inactivating Wnt signaling does not regulate the mRNA expression levels of tkv and other BMP pathway components in ISCs.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data showing no changes in BMP pathway component expression.
